owner: CC owns the code and the proofs. Akien designed the protocol in conversation (2026-08-06 origin, 2026-08-24 settled design) and owns the intention.
children: idle-detection-trigger — the '3 hours without a human' screensaver-like trigger on the cairn device. Code-seam at devices/cairn/.
token-rotation-mechanism — token posting on the announce feed, per-device probe pattern, alpha-order forwarding, and cycle completion detection. Code-seam at devices/cairn/.

questions.a: No separate subscription registry — the rotation is the full alpha device list from the ground loop roster. Every device's probe fires; non-sleeping devices just forward. Settled in conversation: an active 'pass' is just the probe shape (message present → is for us? → no, done; yes → do we sleep? → no → forward), not a poll.

The probe is a design pattern, not a class — a three-line custom probe that matches, decides, and forwards is valid. No shim, no bus routing, no LLM. 'When we were first talking about probes you were trying to give them LLM access, and then it was a complex schema thing' (Akien, 2026-08-24). The base probe covers most things; a custom probe is equally allowed.
Serial by design, parallel deferred to measurement. The OOM history (n=3) and not knowing which cycles are independent settle this for day one.

Held-out devices (those benched by the heartbeat) are not special-cased — their probe fires like anyone else's. If the device is held out, its shim still receives the token and forwards it. The heartbeat's bench is about probes, not about bus messages.

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME:waiting] -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(sleep-rotation-completes) -> PROVED

watchme.trigger: a full alpha-order rotation completes — the token returns to the cairn device after every device has had its turn
watchme.enough: three successful rotations in which at least one device actually ran a sleep cycle (not just forwarded), measured across distinct idle periods
watchme.carrier: the bus record of the complete rotation — all forwarding messages in one cycle, with timestamps, which devices slept and which forwarded, and total cycle duration
watchme.nexus: the cairn device's operational record — did the rotation complete, how long each device took, did any fail or hang
watchme.consumer: the cairn device (operational) + Akien (design validation for the first cycles)
watchme.probe: cairn/devices/cairn/probes/sleep_rotation_completion.py — specifiable but not yet buildable: the cairn device directory does not exist. Depends on the cairn device build (I-the-cairn-device). The probe is created at the WATCHME crossing, after PROVEME.
